verdicts.note: The code confirms it. vid_detect's .equip arm turns every equipment word of 11b into VID_HERC (viddet.inc:588-594), and the scope cut is written out at viddet.inc:527-530. vid_setmode's .herc arm writes 3BFh=1 and 3B8h, then programs vid_6845 with R0=35h (viddet.inc:397-398, 1391-1413). On an MDA the 6845 counts 9-dot characters at about 1.806 MHz, so 54 totals give about 33.4 kHz, against the 18.4 kHz the card was built for. On a Hercules in graphics mode the characters are 16 dots, which gives about 18.8 kHz, so the table is correct only there. The discrimination the fix needs already exists for the secondary card only. vid_memchk's 0x1000 alias test is at vidsel.inc:131-180, and vid_probe_avail retries it with 3BFh=1 at vidsel.inc:231-253. That retry is exactly why the fix must write 3BFh first: an unconfigured Hercules aliases like an MDA. vid_memchk is .ovl on kern_big and .boot2 on kern_small (vidsel.inc:110-128), so the claim that the kern_big blob needs its own copy is right. Writing 3BFh on a real MDA is harmless, because the MDA does not decode that port. The B800 probe cannot be fooled by the Hercules page 1, which stays disabled (3BFh bit 1 clear). The fall-through to VID_CGA can rely on vid_cga_equip (viddet.inc:1466-1496).

All three mechanisms are in the code. (1) ld_check_hdr bounds the image only to at least LD_HDR_SIZE and to at most APP_MAX_SIZE, and the file only through the image-against-file ladder (loader.inc:445-500). Step 6a builds the clear prefix in BX, up to 32+64+16+16+192=320 bytes (1018-1035), then does `sub cx,bx / sub dx,bx` with no carry check (1066-1067) and hands DX straight to lz_decomp_x as its output bound. With image=64 and every prefix flag set, DX is 0xFF00 and CX wraps too. (2) ld_where takes R=roundup512(image-file) (858-889), and nothing checks R+file against ld_alloc's roundup512(img+bss) (1168-1180). The code's own comment says 'a foreign header can, by up to 512 bytes, and nothing here refuses it'. For image=64, file=48 and bss=0, the read alone lands at offset 512 of a 512-byte region. (3) The swap re-check (1093-1094) calls ld_check_hdr again. That rewrites [ld_img]/[ld_bss] through ld_hdr_size (380-385), whose only bound is APP_MAX_SIZE. Then ld_start's `rep stosb` at [ld_img] for [ld_bss] bytes (1303-1307) is never compared with [ld_need]. The fix works as written. ld_check_hdr is the one routine that steps 3, 6 (the re-check) and the image arm (1886) all reach, so a refusal there owes no unreserve on steps 3 and 1886. On a successful exit DX still holds img+bss from ld_hdr_size, because the cfmt tail touches only AL/CL (504-524). So `cmp dx,[ld_need] / ja` after the re-check is a correct test. The re-check runs on the in-region header, which keeps its compression flags, and [ld_fsz] is unchanged, so the new R+file test passes again for a legitimate package.

verdicts.note: The INT 0 is real. wm_ptr2idx does `sub ax,wm_wins / mov cl,WIN_SIZE / div cl` (wm.inc:7259-7263, a few lines above the cited range), so the quotient overflows for AX >= 256*74 = 18,944 (WIN_SIZE 74 on kern_big, 65 on kern_small, wm.inc:128,133), and that range includes any BX below wm_wins. The unvalidated doors are real as well. wm_show/hide/front go to wm_lk_go and then to their bodies with no check (wm.inc:3298-3330, 3345-3362, 3675, 4368). wm_destroy has no check either (3048). wm_clip_set reaches wm_zabove through wm_clip_occw (6023, 6362-6368). OSAPI_WM_WAKE writes [bx+W_WKQ] with 'BX is trusted' (os88api.inc:1733). What must change is the claim that the +5 bound fixes the hazard. Clamping before the div only swaps a dead machine for silent corruption. A wild BX then maps to slot MAX_WIN-1, which can be a live window. The bodies still write through the wild BX: wm_show_b does `or word [bx+W_FLAGS],2`, and wm_destroy zeroes [bx+W_FLAGS] and [bx+W_WKQ] (about 3070) and then drops the clamped slot's save-under and z-order entry. So it unlinks another package's live window. To contain it, put wm_isrec (wm.inc:11655, which already handles both ends with one unsigned compare) at the SHOW, HIDE, FRONT, DESTROY and CLIP_SET doors with a CF refusal. That is wm-13's fix, and it belongs in this item's Fix, not only at the wake. With the bound in front of the div, the existing post-div clamp can never fire. The wm-2 alternative has the same limit: the bounded load reads through the wild BX and clamps, so it also needs the door checks.

The foundations are real. inst_task_die takes the gfx lock and then far-calls desk_drop_x on the dying worker (instance.inc:1929-1948). cur_shape_pass far-calls DKD_HOVER with no lock (ui.inc:1003-1010). mod_disarm's own comment admits the drop can run while the UI task is inside a slot, and it guards only against a torn slot (mod.inc:879-886). FCP_MOD and FDLG_MOD exist only under KERN_SMALL (kernel.asm:1093-1113). kernresident.py does exclude MEM_PG_MIN..MAX claims from the resident total (tests/kernresident.py:84-94), and MEM_PG_LOW=0xFC is in that range (memory.inc:355-358), so the gauge accounting holds. Four things in the claim need to change. (1) 'That answers ONDEMAND-PLAN 1.2/1.3's system-disk objection' is overstated. It holds only while the claim survives. A MEM_PG_LOW claim is shed exactly when the heap is tight: on kern_big's 128KB rule-3 machine, or any time a big package launches. After that, Save As, the chooser and Copy on kern_big fail with 'Needs Sys Disk A:' while the user's disk is in the drive. kern_big has never had that failure, so this is a user-visible behaviour change that needs the owner's decision. The Risk section's mention is not enough. (2) 'kern_small already ships the same bodies' is false for FDLG. fdlg.inc carries kern_big-only arms: FDH_RECT instead of PAINT/CLICK/UP (fdlg.inc:70-76, 933-937), FDX dskw_czsize (653), DESK.DRV's DKD_KEY hook (746-760), and FDX fm_btn1 (1056). That is 2,080 .cold on kern_big against FDLG.DRV's 1,191. A kern_big module arm with its own entry and FDX set is new seam work, not a flag flip. (3) ROM_COLD is on by default (kernel.asm:1115-1131). On a machine whose .cold is adopted by the ROM or COLDHMA.SYS, these bodies already cost no conventional RAM, and the preload would add a ~4KB heap claim there. (4) The disk cost is missing. A reload after a shed needs FILECP.DRV/FDLG.DRV files on all four kern_big system-disk geometries (or a re-read of a packed slice of KERNEL.SYS), and the boot read grows by the ~6 sectors either way. The kern_mega exclusion and the byte arithmetic (-3,600 +108..192 = -3,492..-3,408) are consistent.

AT rung: the PS/2 code is already refused on CPU_8086 (mouse.inc:1844, 1646-1650). The mechanism is real; I checked it against the built images. KERNEL.SYS starts at LBA 14 on os8088-360/720, 29 on -120, 33 on os8088.img and 12 on small360/720 (BPBs read from build/*.img). kern_big's 13-sector blob puts .text at LBA 27 = head 1 sector 1 on 360/720. So run 27..35, and under KZIP the 9-sector plain head (boot2.asm:341-344), lies on head 1 only. File sector 21 (Makefile:1021, 4096+13*512) = LBA 35 never sits past a flip, so the canary is inert there. t_canary.crosses() starts at `data` (tests/unit/t_canary.py:112), sees run 18..35 and wrongly passes.

Splash half confirmed: vid_setmode is at .text 0x7F5 and gfx_rowbase at 0x8C4 (build/kernel.map:3335,3347). spw_resident_end is 0x922, and 0x842 on smallk. On 1.2MB .text starts at head 0 sector 13 and crosses at .text sector 3. On small360/720 it starts at head 0 sector 6 and crosses at .text sector 4. spl_tick (boot2.asm:356-377) runs before the canary (419-473). Only 1.44MB is protected.

KSIG_OFF 22528 (file sector 57) checks out on all six images, with the KZ head split and DMA pages modelled. LBAs 71/71/86/90/69/69 each sit past the flip of their cylinder run, and the tail lands at linear 0x6000 (big) / 0x4000 (small), so no 64KB split comes before it. Sector sums differ from both neighbours in kernel.sys, smallk and megak.

Three corrections:
(1) The KSIG_OFF change is NOT 0 bytes on kern_big. 22528 >= KZ_HEADSEC*512 turns on the `%if KSIG_OFF >= KZ_HEADSEC * 512` ES adjustment at boot2.asm:436-454 and 465-467: push es, push ax, mov ax,es, add ax,KZ_RPARA, mov es,ax, pop ax, pop es. That is about +11 .boot2, which today's 4096 never assembles (kern_small's 5120 already does). Total .boot2 is about +19 against boot-7's -41. It still fits.
(2) Making crosses() start at data+BOOT2_SECS is not enough. Under KZIP the tail restarts at kernel start + KZ_HEADSEC, so the real run partition also splits there. On 1.44MB the tail run 55..71 is head-1-only, yet a data+B walk would call it crossing. crosses() must model the head split (and the DMA-page bound) as well as the blob.
(3) Keeping the track bound for the head adds one int 13h (about one revolution) on FOUR geometries, not one. The 9-sector head crosses a head on small360, small720, 1.2MB and 1.44MB (LBA 23..31, 42..50, 46..54); only big 360/720 cost nothing. State that boot-time cost.

That arm calls dsk_dest_b0 with DX = [di+FS_VSEG] (files.inc:1693-1715), and dsk_dest_x stores [dsk_dseg] (disk.inc:8605-8610). The mount's step 2 runs dsk_rah_want (disk.inc:4262), which claims MEM_P_DIRW at HIGH, and dsk_fatw_want (4288 -> 5997-6005), which claims MEM_P_FATW at MED and gates on mem_avail_lvl at its own rank, counting cheaper caches as free. Both outrank MEM_P_VIEW at LOW (memory.inc:373,394,439). mem_shed_one picks the cheapest record below the claimant (memory.inc:1420-1445), and mem_pg_forget's .view arm, KERN_SMALL only (memory.inc:1486-1489,1519-1523), calls fmv_demote. fmv_demote clears FS_VSEG/[fm_vseg] and never [dsk_dseg] (files.inc:1410-1437). Step 3 then writes through `mov es,[dsk_dseg]` (disk.inc:4440). The proposed fix is sufficient for that reason: skip a record whose MC_SEG (offset 0, memory.inc:77) equals [dsk_dseg], beside the mem_fatw_dirty test. Implementation note: DL carries the level into `mov al,dl`, so compare through another register, for example CX. About 9-10 bytes of .cold.

Confirmed. The guards at vga12.inc:1896-1899 are `or cx,cx / jz vga_b4out` and `or dx,dx / jz`. They run before the region walk and the hook. The planar gate (vga12.inc:2056-2066) does `mov dx,ax / add dx,cx / cmp dx,[vid_cw] / ja`, and with x=20, w=0xFFF6 that wraps to 10 and passes. `cmp cx,16 / jb` is unsigned and passes, so gfx_blit_pok = 1. The 1bpp gate (2016-2020) wraps the same way. In vga_blit_prow, BX = 20+0xFFF6-1 = 9 gives DI = 1 and DX = 2, so n = 1-2+1 = 0. BP = 0, and the dec/jnz loop runs 65,536 groups from vga_pbuf in DS = VGABUF_SEG (or mega_vbsel on kern_mega). gfx_blitp carries the jle form (vga12.inc:2866-2870; the synth's line cite is about 10 lines off). jz->jle is the same 2-byte short Jcc. After OR, OF = 0, so jle catches zero and negative alike, and no legal width or height reaches 0x8000. Fixing dx's guard too also covers the negative-height row loop.

verdicts.note:
The mechanism is confirmed. drv_wcnt is one byte (driver.inc:6132), increased and decreased at spawn and exit (4592, 4617). drv_unload_x calls DETACH, waits 91 ticks on the global count, and on timeout jumps to .out, skipping drv_release (driver.inc:4157-4185). So the row stays loaded and its class published after a successful detach. drv_shutdown_x unloads rows in order (4199-4212), so each row before USBMOUSE pays 5 s at reboot. memory.inc:2143 pins on any non-zero count.

The population is wrong. USBMOUSE.DRV spawns its worker only on the CH375 arm (Book8088, ports 0x260/0x261). um_ready says `cmp byte [um_pm],0 / jne um_ok`, and the comment reads "a PicoMEM's mouse arrives by interrupt: no chip to poll, so no worker" (drivers/usbmouse/usbmouse.asm:139-141). So the stall happens on a Book8088 with its CH375 mouse up, NOT on 'every PicoMEM USB-mouse machine', which has no driver worker at all. Restate L accordingly.

The fix is incomplete. Per-row counts remove USBMOUSE's cross-talk. For a genuinely stuck worker, the timeout path should also clear DRVR_ENT (or mark the row detached) as well as unpublishing the class. Otherwise the next untick calls DRVV_DETACH a second time (driver.inc:4157-4160) and the stale-vector restore the claim cites remains.

histsys-7 is real: drv_svc is DSV_SIZE*(DRVC_MAX-3) = 7x36 = 252 bytes on kern_big (driver.inc:6166, DRVC_MAX 10 at :217) and 2x36 = 72 on kern_small (DRVC_MAX 5 at :219). drv_publish zeroes the copy and then copies only DRV_H_DSV&3Fh bytes (driver.inc:4048-4087). Three things must change.

(1) drivers-10 + bytes-8 break a resident reader the WP does not name. osapi_img_name (kernel.asm:6439-6515) is the kern_big .cold body of an OSAPI cell, used by the Task Manager. At any time it walks drv_tab, ss_row, xm_row and mod_tab, then copies the NUL string at [row+DRVR_FILE] / MODR_FILE (kernel.asm:6505; layout asserted at :8694). kern_mega's mega_imgnf answers the same question. So the claim that the names are 'read only by drv_load_at' and image-resident loaders is false. If DRVR_FILE becomes an offset into an image-only DRV_FILES table, the Task Manager gets garbage. If the .DRV suffix is stripped from mod_f_* (bytes-8), modules are named without '.DRV'. Either keep the names resident on kern_big, which drops about -120 of the kern_big total, or price a rework of osapi_img_name and mega_imgnf first. kern_small has no osapi_img_name (it is %ifdef KERN_BIG), so its -46 is unaffected.

(2) The service table is not at a fixed place in the driver. It is wherever DRVV_ATTACH's SI pointed (driver.inc:3995-3998; publish 'SI = its service table offset' :4016). Reading in place therefore has to keep that offset for each class: about +12 .bss for six classes, which the synth's 'read the rest in place at [es:di+DSV_*]' leaves out. The source finding states it. Sites that hold ES for a transfer must also bank ES around the read (the drv_blk_call/drv_fs_call paths, where ES:BX or DX:BX is the buffer).

(3) drivers-5. The area verifier's correction says drv_unload_x relies on the BX rule too, so the push/pop belongs there as well, not only in %1_call and drv_call_ent. Deleting 'PRESERVE BX' from os88drv.inc with no DRV_VER bump lets a driver written to the new text clobber BX on an older DRV_VER-12 kernel, where drv_attach reads the row through BX. Either keep the sentence for portability ('the kernel banks BX from build N; preserve it to run on older kernels') or treat the deletion as a bump.

The abi-5 and isr-11 text items stand.

Revised bytes: kern_big about -70..-125 (histsys-7 -78..-128, drivers-13 -4, drivers-5 +4..6), not -202..-262, unless osapi_img_name is reworked. kern_small -46 stands.

verdicts.note:
The mechanism is confirmed:

- wm_ptr2idx is `sub ax,wm_wins / mov cl,WIN_SIZE / div cl` (wm.inc:7258-7281). Its own comment says the div raises INT 0 for an offset past 256*WIN_SIZE or below the table.
- wm_destroy is OSAPI_RSLOT (kernel.asm:3219-3220). It reaches wm_su_drop and wm_ptr2idx with no inst_wchk (wm.inc:3048-3077).
- inst_wchk's own banner says 'int 0, no handler installed' (instance.inc:1984-1986).
- The 19→11 byte count is exact: 19 for the current body, 11 for `mov al,[bx+W_IDX]`, the bound, cbw and ret.
- The IBM-ROM consequence rests on the project's own instrumented row (docs/TESTING.md:186-189, tests/int0sweep.py). On a 286 a divide error is a fault, so the IRET re-runs the DIV.

One side effect is not mentioned. WIN_SIZE 74→75 on kern_big (wm.inc:128-131) makes the record stride odd, so every other window's word fields (W_X..W_ONWH) become odd-aligned. That costs nothing on the 8088 target, but each word access pays an extra bus cycle on 8086/286/386, which is exactly the hardware kern_big's 286+ machines and kern_mega run on. That eats into the claimed per-damage-pass win there. Either pad to 76 (+MAX_WIN bytes .bss on kern_big) or state the trade. kern_small goes 65→66 and becomes aligned.

The synth's other notes stand: W_IDX must sit outside wm_create's W_MENUS..WIN_SIZE zero run (wm.inc:105-108), and os88geom.py and t_mirror must follow.

verdicts.note:
The pieces exist as described.

- ld_hdr_ok's version test is an equality (loader.inc:292-296).
- 0060:0006-0007 is zero padding today, and the comment confirms the historical caveat the synth carries: 'the mouse instrument used to have a fixed word at 0x0006 and is now an entry in the registry at 0x000E' (kernel.asm:2349-2351).
- Header byte 31 is the 16th name byte. OS88_HEADER refuses names over 15 characters (apps/os88api.inc:4383-4387), and os88pkg.parse_name fails a field with no NUL or with non-NUL bytes after the terminator (tools/os88pkg.py:114-126). So byte 31 is 0 in every package.
- There is a precedent for giving byte 31 a meaning: the driver header already uses its byte 31 as the bss count, 'FREE because the name at +16 is capped at 15 characters' (driver.inc:362-366).
- The kernel's package-name readers are all bounded at 15: inst_set_name_x copies at most 15 (instance.inc:1242-1250), and stikmenu.inc:410-414 uses cx=15 plus a NUL. A 15-character name with a non-zero level byte is therefore read correctly.

Two points belong in the implementation and do not falsify the claim. os88pkg.py's 'non-NUL bytes after the terminator' check must exempt byte 31. OS88_NEED must compare the cell's OFFSET half, because OSAPI_* names are KERNEL_SEG:offset far-pointer defines. The 'no PKG_FMT-10 kernel predates SPEC 57' caveat is the right one to resolve, given the mouse word history.

The knobs, their byte figures (+32/+38/+34 = +104; +122/+39/+21 = +182 .vga) and the XT timings match docs/plans/LAST-DROP-PERF.md 7.1 rows 2-8. I checked by section that every VGASAVE/VGAFILL/VGAEDGE code arm sits in .vga (vga12.inc:3408-3877, 4417-4450, 4749-4814; mouse.inc:4600-4798). The VGASAVE arms in .text are comment-only (vga12.inc:4332/4370/4487-4697, mouse.inc:4871/5107/6148/6271). The block itself is at kernel.asm:291-307, not 283-294.

What must change: 'turn each taken knob's arm unconditional on KERN_BIG and delete its other arm', and 'both arms stop living in wm.inc and softgfx.inc', cannot both hold for the non-VGA rows. Those bodies are shared with kern_small and are not under KERN_BIG:

The diagnosis holds. mem_pg_own is a closed kernel list (kernel/memory.inc:1318-1335). A purgeable flag in bit 13 would read as a head of 0x2000 or more paragraphs. mem_hifit would then reject placements, and the tests at 3800/6623 would treat the claim as DMA-constrained. (2) The shed side cannot call the proc where it would be called. mem_shed_one runs entirely inside pushf/cli (memory.inc:1414-1419), and its notice is a word store through mem_pg_forget. disk.inc:6097/6165 make 'inside mem_shed_one's cli, so word stores and nothing else' a contract. Either have mem_shed_one skip MEMP_PURGEABLE records when reached from mem_regrow, or defer their purge to the compactor's drop arm only. Name mem_cp_busy, or an equivalent, as set across the purge call, so that a proc which claims or regrows is refused (memory.inc:4589-4592).

The other parts are not affected: hm-11's init-drop via the KEEP re-home, hm-13, files RT2 and the os88lmem lift. Minor: the claim says 'four packages' hand-roll sub-allocators, while systemic.md lists three (WIN16, Sheet, Weave).

The item does not mention one limit, and the AT hook needs one guard. sch_switch refuses to switch while SS is not LOW_SEG (sched.inc ~2425, the SPEC.md 8.5 test). On a BIOS that serves int 13h on its own stack (SeaBIOS under QEMU/Bochs, per mouse.inc:413-425 and sched.inc:2214-2222), releasing sch_lock therefore buys nothing. The int 15h AH=90h hook would also be entered on that foreign stack.

The hook must test SS == LOW_SEG and otherwise return to the BIOS's own wait (CF=0), not call task_sleep. Calling task_sleep there would mean a refused switch inside a sleep, or a task record banking a ROM stack. It must also act only on AL=01h (diskette); AH=90h is issued for the keyboard too. State that the benefit is real on the IBM/XT ROMs, which keep the caller's stack, and conditional elsewhere. Also carry ctx-3's second hazard explicitly: nothing enforces SPEC.md 20.6 rule 7, the only thing that stops a second task entering dsk_xfer while the UI task is in the ROM.

(1) +15 bit 5 is NOT a free bit. LD_H_CLASS is a 6-bit class index: inst_pkg_spawn does `and bx,0x3F` (instance.inc:2106-2107), and sched.inc:2891-2893 states it in an %error. With bit 5 set, every kernel shipped so far reads index >= 32 and gives SCH_STACK, the largest class (instance.inc:2116-2118). A 'clean' package therefore silently loses its declared 128/192 class on every real-mode kernel: +128..256 LOW_SEG bytes per worker. That is safe but not free. Either narrow the mask to 1Fh in the same change and accept that old kernels over-allocate, or put the bit somewhere else.

(2) The level is package-only. Drivers already use +31 as bss paragraphs (tools/os88drv.py:41-45, :137-140, :193; tools/os88rom.py:1025), and drivers share ld_hdr_ok (driver.inc:3644). The compare must stay in ld_check_hdr (loader.inc:962/1094/1886), never in ld_hdr_ok.

- os88disk.py:289-293 fails 'non-printable bytes in header name field' for a 15-char name.

Once the purgeable claims are shed under pressure, Save/Open or a copy on a single-drive XT asks for the system disk mid-task. The -3.4KB is honest by KERN_BUDGET's 'non-purgeable' definition, but the trade should be stated, along with the pin held open-to-close.

KBMOUSE has the same issue. input R2's premise, 'the system disk is in the drive at that moment on every machine that has no mouse', is not guaranteed after a swap on a one-drive machine. There the keyboard mouse is the ONLY pointer, so the first press would be refused until the user reinserts the system disk. kbm_key runs on the UI task (ui.inc:214; mouse.inc:2463), so a module is mechanically fine. kbm_isr is IRQ1's handler for the whole kernel (mega.inc:507) and must stay resident; R2's move list already excludes it, so keep it that way.

The DMA-head defect is real and still live: kernel/memory.inc:872-878 is `mov si,cx / mov cl,6 / shl si,cl / pop cx / jnc .set`, so CF is bit 10 alone. Two corrections. (1) There are three package doors, not four, and two of them are already fixed: claim AX at memory.inc:939 (`cmp ax,1024 / jae .big`) and regrow at :4584. md-16 is kerndos/kdshim.inc:418-422, kern_dos's private allocator. kern_dos has no OSAPI table, and its callers are kernel-internal constants (kdgate.inc:95-97 `mov ax, KD_GATE_KB`). Withdrawing the package cells does not touch it. (2) 'The paragraph door has no shift' only holds if the KERNEL's own KB callers convert as well, and C1 does not scope them. The 217 count is OSAPI_* package sites only. The internal callers that still enter the KB entries include: disk.inc:9674 and :9922 (mem_regrow); files.inc:1306, :1821 and :6071 (files.inc:1309 also keeps FS_VKB in KB); hiber.inc:2094, :2605, :2930 and :4047 (`mov bp, mem_claim_x`); mega.inc:415 and font.inc:375 (mem_claim_hi_x); diskops.inc:3195-3197; filecp.inc:801-803 (FCPX mem_claim_dma_x); desksc.inc:1183 (mem_regrow); ascw.inc:122. Without converting those, the shifts at mem_claim_x, mem_regrow and mem_claim_dma_x survive, and the '~10-14 KB shifts' part of the bytes and the correctness argument both fall away. Amend to: three package doors, two already guarded. Take mem-5/hm-6's +3 fix now whatever happens to C1. Either add the roughly 20 internal sites to the conversion, or cut the bytes to the cells and mmf thunks only.

The premise that HDD.DRV and EMS.DRV declare short tables is false. hdd.asm:1542-1573 lists 18 cells, DSV_CAPS through DSV_PKGCALL. That is 36 bytes, which is DSV_SIZE (os88drv.inc:366 and :419). ems.asm:485-487 gives em_svc_end - em_svc = (em_door+2) - (em_door-DSV_PKGCALL) = 36. The built headers agree: byte +15 of build/hdd.bin and build/ems.bin is 0xA4, which is a length of 36; sound.bin is the same, and ether.bin is 0xE4, also 36. FSV +10 is 30 = FSV_SIZE in all four. So no tree driver pads. Second, deleting drv_publish's zero-fill and clamp (driver.inc:4049-4078) contradicts 'table growth still needs no bump'. The first cell added after the floor needs the tail zero-filled and the +15 length read again, and the clamp is still needed for a driver built against a newer SDK. For the same reason, histsys-7's in-place reads still need a length test for any post-floor cell. Amend to: at the bump, refuse a driver below the floor, which every shipped driver already meets. N1's 0=28 fallbacks (driver.inc:2979-2981, :4071-4072) then go. The zero-fill and clamp stay unless every later growth takes a bump. Re-price D4 to about the fallbacks alone, and drop 'HDD/EMS pad'. Note also that DRV_VER is 12 today (os88drv.inc:711), so '14' presumes a 13.

Confirmed: drv_release frees the image with no IVT test (driver.inc:4232-4351, which reaches mem_free_x unconditionally), and sched_stop restores 0:20h blindly (sched.inc:656-661). But the flag-day savings are overstated. (a) 'Deletes the post-detach IVT scan': no such scan exists. It is drivers-6's proposed +25 now-fix, so the -25 .cold is real only if that fix is taken first. (b) 'Deletes the image-move IVT walk': mem_rr_ivt (memory.inc:3495-3505) also covers int 33h, which is USBMOUSE's PicoMEM vector and not an IRQ line. It also covers vectors held by moved PACKAGE regions; mem-7 cites DOS.O88's int 08h chain at apps/dos/dos.asm:11445. And kern_mega's mem_ivt_relocf walks it (memory.inc:3186-3214). A mandatory DRV_VER cell binds drivers only, so the walk cannot be deleted. At best it becomes a registry-driven rewrite, which still rewrites the IVT when an image moves. To delete it, the cell must also cover int 33h and package hooks (os88spk's IRQ0 bracket, DOS's IVT exchange), which needs PKG_FMT and not only DRV_VER. Amend the flag-day row to 'replaces the walk for driver IRQ lines', and add int 33h and package hooks to the scope or say they stay.

DRV_CALL's no-driver path is confirmed (driver.inc:6652-6656: `xor ax,ax / stc`), as are kern_mega's stc sled (fsx.inc:2341-2351) and XREFUSE answering 1 (kernel.asm:2600-2604). Three gaps. (1) The stream stub's AX=4 is deliberate (snd.inc:707-712: 'AX = 4 "no streaming sink"... AX = 0 is how every stream verb says OK'), and Recorder reads it at apps/recorder/recorder.asm:754 (`cmp ax, 4 ; 4 = no streaming sink at all`). Making AX=1 universal would break Recorder, so either name 4 as a kept family code or put it in the census. (2) Turning the bare stc stubs into AX=1 clobbers a register those cells preserve today. osapi_snd_fm (snd.inc:714-717) serves FM, xm_free and vol_stat. FM takes AL as its verb (os88api.inc:561-573), and there are 50 OSAPI_SND_FM sites in apps/. A caller that issues note-ons without reloading AL would, after one refusal, issue verb 1 (note-off). The census must cover reliance on AX surviving a CF=1, not only readers of AX=0. (3) 'Most stubs share XREFUSE' does not work as written. XREFUSE is an inline far cell ending in retf (OSAPI_IEND, kernel.asm:2573-2574), and the kernel stubs are near procs reached through api_rs, so they need a shared near `mov ax,1/stc/ret` tail. kern_mega's sled needs an AX=1 tail per gap, or within short-jump range of every gap, so that part is not ~0. Keep the doc half now, and widen the census and the byte estimate.

L7's kernel half checks out: instance.inc:2106-2116 masks with 0x3F and answers an out-of-range index with the largest class. So bit 5 on an old kernel means a bigger stack and no refusal, and new kernels must mask with 0x1F. But the build refuses the bit today. tools/os88pkg.py:211 fails any package with `a[15] & 0x3F > STK_CLASS_MAX` (4), so a bit-5 package does not pass the validator. os88pkg.py must mask 0x1F as well, and it is one of fork rule 6's shipped-byte writers. sched.inc:2891-2893's %error text and the SDK header macro move with it, so os88api.inc's fingerprint changes and needs `abilock --update` (no bump). That makes it more than a '+12 .mega, kern_mega only' change. Also, 'D8 supplies the IRQ half' overstates it. mega_null0 (mega.inc:4831-4842) traps EVERY segment-0 DS/ES access, BDA reads included; packages read the BDA (win16's w16user.inc and w16i21.inc, video.asm reference 0x46C/0x417) and hook vectors (DOS.O88). A driver-only IRQ cell retires only the drivers' hooking share of mega_null0/mega_db. Package BDA and IVT access still needs an MEGA_SEG0-style SDK path before a 'clean' package can forbid the fixup. [mega_kfix] does not exist yet; it is correctly framed as proposed.

The mechanism is real and the byte arithmetic holds: 112 rare cells x (6-2) = -448, then +45 door, +6 tails, +12 promotions gives about -385. A site goes from 5 bytes to 3 (CD nn idx). retf 2 discards the stacked FLAGS, so the routine's CF/ZF survive. Package code selectors on kern_mega are readable (0x9A, mega.inc:9914, 10662), so the index can be fetched there. Five things must change:
(1) The citation is wrong. kernel.asm:2501-2513 is the OSAPI_RCELL macro family. The bodies are api_rx/api_x (kernel.asm:4588-4605), api_rxc (4611), api_rsc/api_rs (4632-4650) and api_rn (4739).
(2) The bodies do not run 'unchanged'. Each starts with the cell-specific 'pop bp / mov bp,[cs:bp]', so the door must enter past it. Each ends in retf. api_x.done is shared with every hot OSAPI_XCELL ('jmp strict near api_x', kernel.asm:2475-2479), so the X family needs a second retf 2 tail and cannot simply rewrite the one it has.
(3) The past-the-end CF=1 covers RARE indices only. A newer HOT cell called on an older kernel is still a wild far call past osapi_table_end. So loader-6's run-time hole is closed only for rare cells, and A4 is still needed for the hot ones.
(4) The vector rule is backwards for windowed DOS. Being outside the exchange set (dosw.inc:75-80) means a windowed DOS program's direct IVT write to that vector is NOT banked away, and would capture every package's rare calls while it runs. An 8088 cannot catch a direct write. 'Above 3Fh' is also not enough on its own: 40h (XT diskette relocation, mega.inc:454-459), 41h/46h, 4Ah, 67h (EMS) and 70h-77h (slave PIC, and kern_mega's own remap at megados.inc:1922-1927) are all above 3Fh. Name the range.
(5) Not mentioned: kern_mega's real-mode FSX bracket (fsx.inc:2337-2360) today refuses every non-kept cell by filling the table with stc/retf. Under T5 the rare cells are not in the table, so the bracket must also point IVT[door] at a refusal that ends in retf 2. The IDT is also built from the IVT (mega.inc:654-672), so how a door gate is built there needs specifying.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: ~-385 .text kern_big/kern_mega(conv), ~-245 kern_small (ESTIMATED); kern_big +~6 more for a second X tail beside api_x.done; -2 x 2,736 package sites (MEASURED). The run-time refusal covers rare cells only.

verdicts.note:
The pads are confirmed from the maps. build/kernel.map has .bss ending at 0xB27E, giving 386 to 0xB400. build/smallk has 0x80CB, giving 309. build/megak has 0xC918, giving 232. FAT_SEG equ KERNEL_SEG + KIMG_PARA is at kernel.asm:1804. That is the ROM_COLD arm, which is on by default (kernel.asm:1131); 1806 is the NO_ROM_COLD A/B. The image is rounded today because dsk_secbuf is LOW_SEG's first bytes and is a transfer base (dskwin.inc:292-306). Moving it below KERNEL_SEG is therefore what frees the rounding, so the mechanism is real. Three things must change:
(1) kern_mega has no LADDER_PACK. It is gated on ROM_ADOPT (kernel.asm:1172-1176), which kern_mega does not define (1143-1146). Its rungs above the image stay 512-multiples and COLD_SEG stays a multiple of 8 paragraphs. So 232 is the image pad, not a measured conventional saving. ABI-BREAK-LIST's own L1 row says to measure kern_mega's figure before quoting it.
(2) On kern_big and kern_small, KERN_END rounds once to 512 (kernel.asm:1903-1906). KERN_SIZE therefore moves by 0 or 512 depending on today's top pad; my ladder estimate gives a full 512 on kern_big today. Quoting the pad is the right bytes-not-rungs figure, but 'MEASURED -386 resident' should say it is a byte figure, not a KERN_SIZE delta.
(3) 'Churn falls to the hot SLOTs, ES-on-callback and the tools' undercounts. Packages hold about 150 explicit 'mov ax, KERNEL_SEG' sites (for example apps/pixelstein/pxwin.inc:198 and apps/sheet/sheet.asm:4267). There are also the published fixed addresses 0060:000C and 0060:000E, plus crt0, DOS/kerndos, the boot paths, hibernate images, ROMs and COLDHMA. Most are rebuilds rather than edits, but the stored artefacts are not.
Cross-item: A4's '0060:0006' becomes KERNEL_SEG:0006 = 01A0:0006 after L1.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: -386 / -309 bytes (the pad, MEASURED; KERN_SIZE moves 0 or 512 by build) on kern_big/kern_small; kern_mega: 232-byte pad, conventional saving UNMEASURED (rungs stay 512-rounded and COLD_SEG 8-paragraph aligned)

verdicts.note:
The facts are confirmed. kern_big's record has 13 handler words: PAINT, ONKEY, ONCLICK, ONSIZE, ONMOUSEUP, ONDRAG and ONTIMER at 12-31, then ONSZ, ONWK, ONCL, ONRC, ABOUT and ONWH in the side block (wm.inc:113-127). kern_small has 10 (W_SIDE=28, wm.inc:103). No package or driver reads or writes a handler word through the record: a grep of apps/ and drivers/ for memory operands on W_PAINT..W_ONWH finds none outside os88api.inc; Sticky Apps and deskclok go through the setters (os88stik.inc:987-1001, deskclok/dkset.inc:230-233). There are six MEGA_ICWB/ICWBW handler-setter stubs (kernel.asm:2858, 3341, 3611, 3707, 4180, 4311; mega.inc:5643-5648). Kernel windows have W_SEG=0 and callbacks in .cold (wm.inc:375-378), so kernel class tables in .cold fit the dispatcher if the helper takes COLD_SEG when W_SEG=0. The kernel has 29 handler-field references (wm 11, ui 8, ctrl 2, files 2, menu 1, fdlg 1, kernel.asm 4), which matches the '28 dispatch reads' scale.
What must change is the per-callback cost. Today it is one '[si+W_x]' load. Under R14 it is a segment load (W_SEG or COLD_SEG), a W_CLASS load, a length-byte compare and branch, and a slot load. On an 8088 that is about +50 to +70 clocks, PREDICTED, not +~20.
Also say that the class-table length byte must cover every slot the kernel can read on the largest kernel. Otherwise a table that is short on purpose silently drops ONWH, the last slot.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: ~-215 kern_big, ~-95 kern_small, ~-270 kern_mega conv under T5 (ESTIMATED); ~-1.5KB unpacked across packages; +~50-70 clocks a callback (PREDICTED)

verdicts.note:
The mechanism holds. 0x06-0x07 is free padding, but the citation is kernel.asm:2349-2352, not 2357-2359. ld_check_hdr (loader.inc:428) is .cold and already returns LD_EVER through ld_hdr_ok (loader.inc:293-299), so about +8 is plausible. Every package built today has byte 31 = 0: I checked every 'O8' .bin under build/, and the longest name is 13 characters. Three things must change:
(1) Byte 31 is the NUL terminator of a legal 15-character name. os88pkg.py:122 allows up to 15, and os88pkg.py:124 refuses any non-NUL byte after the terminator. A nonzero level there would leave a 15-character name unterminated, both for this validator and for the kernel's name readers (stikmenu.inc:410 'the program name, as the loader copies it'). So the change must also cap names at 14 (os88pkg.py:122 and SPEC.md 20.2's header contract) and relax the :124 check for byte 31. Packages already built with 15-character names keep byte31=0, which reads as level 0 and is harmless.
(2) Name the word KERNEL_SEG:0006, not 0060:0006, because L1 moves KERNEL_SEG to 0x01A0.
(3) It closes the hole only on kernels that carry it, as stated. T5's run-time half covers rare cells only, so A4 is the only guard for newer hot cells.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: 0 resident (kernel word in existing padding); ~+8 .cold in ld_check_hdr; os88pkg name cap 15->14 (host); no bump (abilock --update)

verdicts.note:
A byte-identical rewrite is real. OSAPI_* names are %defines of KERNEL_SEG:offset (os88api.inc:309-310), so 'OSCALL %1' emitting 'call %1' assembles the same bytes. I count 6,998 'call OSAPI_' in apps/+drivers asm/inc against the claimed 6,954, close enough. There are no 'jmp OSAPI_' tail-call sites to break T5's later flip, so the cmp proof works for the BINARIES. Two things must change:
(1) It is not '0, source only': a set of host gates parse the literal text 'call OSAPI_X' and would silently match nothing after the rewrite. Some would go vacuously green, some would fail on stale ratchet entries. Examples: t_textrules.py:50 (the transparent-text ratchet), t_movable.py:76 and :87 (the region-movable ratchet), t_stkclass.py:67 (SPAWN), t_megahigh.py:109, t_pins.py:144 and :201, t_drvclaim.py:58 and :157, and t_toast.py's call-following. Each must learn OSCALL in the same commit and be broken on purpose to show it still goes red (docs/WRITING-TESTS.md §1). cmp of the images cannot see any of this.
(2) After T5 flips the macro, a rare name must stop being a far-call address. Otherwise out-of-tree source that still says 'call OSAPI_X' assembles to a wild far call into the renumbered table instead of failing to assemble.
The renames-with-aliases half stands.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: 0 shipped bytes; SDK text (abilock --update, no bump); plus the source gates updated in the same commit (t_textrules, t_movable, t_stkclass, t_megahigh, t_pins, t_drvclaim, t_toast)
